subject: Meditech - Dedicated GPU capacity handoff & implementation checklist
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@meditech.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@meditech.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity requirements and timeline

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency numbers look promising. We are ready to move from PoC to a dedicated GPU pool but I want to make sure we capture the implementation constraints on our side. High level:

- Initial capacity target: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (steady), with a 2x burst window for traffic spikes during batch processing windows.
- Preferred region: us-west-2, but we have an EU regulatory cluster we may want mirrored later.
- Autoscale behavior: aggressive scale-out during nightly batch windows (04:00–06:00 UTC), conservative scale-in (keep warm nodes for 30 min idle).
- Security: we need confirmation of KMS integration and audit log retention for 12 months.

Could you send a short checklist of tasks and owners so we can align our infra team? Also include any lead times for provisioning reserved nodes and expected cost delta for reserved vs burst use.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Barnes
Head of ML Ops, Meditech AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@meditech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity requirements and timeline

Alicia — great to hear. I pulled together a compact handoff/checklist for the dedicated pool rollout and attached an estimate (capacity-estimate-20260914.xlsx). High level answers below; more detail in the attached and Marissa/Dev can expand.

Summary answers:
- Lead time: reserved pool in hosted Dedicated typically 10 business days for a standard 8x A100-equivalent configuration (longer if specific interconnects or on-prem placements required). Burst capacity can be available within 48 hours if quota exists in the region.
- Cost: attached workbook shows steady reserved pricing vs burst hourly; ballpark: reserved ~25% lower per-token cost with committed monthly, bursts pay spot/hourly uplift ~1.6–2.2x depending on utilization.
- KMS & audit logs: supported. We will exchange a KMS key policy and confirm log forwarding to your SIEM; retention configurable up to 24 months.
- Autoscale policy recommendations:
  - Nightly batch window (04:00–06:00 UTC): pre-warm 4 extra GPUs 30 minutes before window.
  - Scale-in cooldown: 30 minutes after idle threshold.
  - Burst cap: hard cap at 2x steady capacity to avoid uncontrolled spend.

Handoff checklist (owners in parens):
1) Provisioning request submitted to capacity team (Rishi) — include exact instance family and region.
2) Networking & VPC peering test (Meditech infra / Marissa) — confirm private connectivity and NAT rules.
3) KMS key exchange & IAM roles (Meditech infra / Dev) — finalize policy for encryption-at-rest.
4) Autoscaling config + cooldown verification (Dev) — apply and run smoke scaling test.
5) Load-profile runbook & prefix cache plan (Marissa) — provide expected token profiles so we can tune batching.
6) Canaries & rollback policy (Rishi/Marissa) — decide if we do a canary in eu-west-1 first or cutover in us-west-2.

Next step: Marissa, Dev — can you add technical tasks & estimated times? Alicia — happy to schedule a 30-min handoff tomorrow to run through the checklist and DocuSign the SLA.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-estimate-20260914.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@meditech.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity requirements and timeline

Thanks — adding the technical checklist and a few configuration notes. I also attached a short one-pager (redwood-dedicated-checklist.pdf) that your infra team can use as a day-of cutover checklist. Key items for our onboarding run: 

- GPU sizing: confirm model variant (we recommend quantized 8-bit variant for inference throughput if your models are compatible; saves ~20–30% token cost).
- KV/Prefix cache: provide 2–3 representative prompt sets (50–200 tokens) so we can validate cache hit-rate; this will inform batching window.
- Monitoring hooks: set up metrics export (Prometheus/Grafana) or provide a read-only CloudWatch role; we need token-level latency breakdown to tune batching.
- Autoscaling testing: recommend a staged test — (1) synthetic token load to validate scale-out, (2) replayed production traffic for 2 hours. We'll run both in a test VPC.

Day-of cutover checklist (short):
- Confirm reserved pool provisioned and network routes validated (Meditech ops).
- Run smoke test: single warm-up prompt + 50 concurrent users.
- Execute batch-window pre-warm and validate throughput.
- Observe scale-in cooldown and ensure no premature terminations.

I'll own the monitoring hooks, Dev will own the autoscaler config, Rishi will coordinate provisioning and legal sign-off.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-checklist.pdf (one-pager)

From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@meditech.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@meditech.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T20:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity requirements and timeline

Marissa / Rishi — this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifying items from our end: 

- EU mirror: we will likely request a mirrored pool in eu-west-1 within 6–8 weeks after the US cutover. Please include estimated lead time and any additional compliance checks.
- Pre-warm: when you say "pre-warm 4 extra GPUs 30 minutes before window", does that assume immediate hot-cache population? We need guidance on how to warm the KV cache without affecting production latency.
- Legal: procurement prefers a 30-day term for the initial reserved commit if that helps with budget approval.

Can we lock a 30-min handoff tomorrow at 10:00 PDT? Ops will join for the VPC/networking items.

Thanks,
Alicia

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@meditech.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity requirements and timeline

Alicia — quick technical notes to address your questions: 

- EU mirror lead time: eu-west-1 typically has similar provisioning lead times (8–12 business days) subject to regional quota. We'll submit parallel requests to shorten elapsed time.
- Cache warm approach: recommended pattern — (1) run a warm-up job that issues representative prompts at low concurrency ~15–30 minutes before the window, populating KV and prefix caches; (2) switch traffic gradually (10% increments) over 10 minutes to ensure steady latency. This avoids a sudden cold-cache spike.
- Pre-warm sizing: pre-warm count assumes workers have an empty KV and will be brought to steady state by the warm-up job. If you already have long-lived sessions, pre-warm can be reduced.
- Autoscaler params (example):
  - scale_out_step: +2 GPUs per evaluation when 95th latency > 350ms for 3 consecutive checks
  - scale_in_cooldown: 30 minutes
  - min_capacity: 8 GPUs
  - max_capacity: 16 GPUs (hard burst cap at 2x)

I'll prepare a gist with the exact HCL/Catalog snippet we use for the autoscaler and post it to the HubSpot deal after the call.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
